explanation shown to learner: Sports and school subjects are uncountable nouns: no article (*play golf, teach maths*). But instruments take *the*: *play the piano*.
explanation in Latvian: Sporta veidi un skolas mācības (matemātika, vēsture) ir neskaitāmi lietvārdi: bez artikula (*play golf, teach maths*). Bet mūzikas instrumentiem vajag *the*: *play the piano*.

task: Choose the correct option: I'm vegetarian. I don't eat ___ meat.
wrong options / checks: the | a
explanation shown to learner: *I'm vegetarian* = meat in general, so no article: *I don't eat meat.* *The meat* would be some particular meat.
explanation in Latvian: *I'm vegetarian* = gaļa vispārīgi, tāpēc bez artikula: *I don't eat meat.* *The meat* būtu kāda noteikta gaļa.

task: Which sentence is correct?
wrong options / checks: Peter is from the Canada. | The Peter is from Canada. | The Peter is from the Canada.
explanation shown to learner: No article with names of people, cities and most countries: *Anna, Riga, Latvia*.
explanation in Latvian: Ar cilvēku, pilsētu un lielākās daļas valstu nosaukumiem artikulu nelieto: *Anna, Riga, Latvia.*

task: Which sentence is correct?
correct answer: My husband plays golf at weekends.
wrong options / checks: My husband plays the golf at weekends. | My husband plays a golf at weekends.
explanation shown to learner: Sports and school subjects are uncountable nouns: no article (*play golf, teach maths*). But instruments take *the*: *play the piano*.
explanation in Latvian: Sporta veidi un skolas mācības (matemātika, vēsture) ir neskaitāmi lietvārdi: bez artikula (*play golf, teach maths*). Bet mūzikas instrumentiem vajag *the*: *play the piano*.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: My parents live in the Spain.
wrong options / checks: We eat fish on Fridays. | Tom collects old cameras. | They live in the UK.
explanation shown to learner: Most countries have no article: *Spain, Latvia*. A few names take *the*: *the UK, the USA*.
explanation in Latvian: Lielākajai daļai valstu artikula nav: *Spain, Latvia.* Daži nosaukumi ir ar *the*: *the UK, the USA*.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: She studies the history at university.
wrong options / checks: Anna and her sister live in Paris. | Horses need a lot of space to run. | I don't drink milk with my coffee.
explanation shown to learner: School subjects in general have no article: *She studies history.* (*the history of Rome* is one particular history.)
explanation in Latvian: Skolas mācībām (vēsture, matemātika) vispārīgi artikula nav: *She studies history.* (*the history of Rome* ir kāda noteikta vēsture.)

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: i drink green tea in the morning
wrong options / checks: also accepted: in the morning i drink green tea
explanation shown to learner: No article with an uncountable noun when we mean it in general: *I don't eat meat.*
explanation in Latvian: Ar neskaitāmu lietvārdu vispārīgā nozīmē artikulu nelieto: *I don't eat meat.*

task: Put the words in order.
explanation shown to learner: No article with a plural noun when we mean all of them in general: *Spiders scare me.* With *the* it would mean some particular ones.
explanation in Latvian: Ar daudzskaitļa lietvārdu vispārīgā nozīmē (visi kopumā) artikulu nelieto: *Spiders scare me.* *the* norādītu uz kādiem noteiktiem.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: my wife and i met in paris
explanation shown to learner: No article with names of people, cities and most countries: *Anna, Riga, Latvia*.
explanation in Latvian: Ar cilvēku, pilsētu un lielākās daļas valstu nosaukumiem artikulu nelieto: *Anna, Riga, Latvia.*

task: Put the words in order to make a question.
explanation shown to learner: No article with an uncountable noun when we mean it in general: *I don't eat meat.* In a question the helping verb (or *am / is / are*) goes before the subject.
explanation in Latvian: Ar neskaitāmu lietvārdu vispārīgā nozīmē artikulu nelieto: *I don't eat meat.* Jautājumā palīgdarbības vārds (vai *am / is / are*) stāv pirms teikuma priekšmeta.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: we want to visit japan next year
wrong options / checks: also accepted: next year we want to visit japan
explanation shown to learner: No article with names of people, cities and most countries: *Anna, Riga, Latvia*.
explanation in Latvian: Ar cilvēku, pilsētu un lielākās daļas valstu nosaukumiem artikulu nelieto: *Anna, Riga, Latvia.*

task: Our new manager is from ___ Sweden.
wrong options / checks: bank: — | the
explanation shown to learner: No article with names of people, cities and most countries: *Anna, Riga, Latvia*.
explanation in Latvian: Ar cilvēku, pilsētu un lielākās daļas valstu nosaukumiem artikulu nelieto: *Anna, Riga, Latvia.*

task: I usually listen to ___ jazz in the car.
wrong options / checks: bank: — | the
explanation shown to learner: Kinds of music in general have no article: *I listen to jazz.* *usually* shows it is a habit, not one particular piece.
explanation in Latvian: Mūzikas veidiem vispārīgi artikula nav: *I listen to jazz.* *usually* rāda, ka tas ir ieradums, nevis kāds noteikts skaņdarbs.

task: I think ___ dogs are better pets than cats.
wrong options / checks: bank: — | the
explanation shown to learner: No article with a plural noun when we mean all of them in general: *Spiders scare me.* With *the* it would mean some particular ones.
explanation in Latvian: Ar daudzskaitļa lietvārdu vispārīgā nozīmē (visi kopumā) artikulu nelieto: *Spiders scare me.* *the* norādītu uz kādiem noteiktiem.

task: My kids spend hours on ___ social media.
wrong options / checks: bank: — | the
explanation shown to learner: No article with an uncountable noun when we mean it in general: *I don't eat meat.*
explanation in Latvian: Ar neskaitāmu lietvārdu vispārīgā nozīmē artikulu nelieto: *I don't eat meat.*

task: Match each beginning with its ending.
correct answer: My cousin lives in = Rome. ; Every morning I drink = orange juice. ; My daughter is afraid of = snakes. ; At weekends we play = volleyball.
explanation shown to learner: No article with names (*Rome*), uncountable nouns (*orange juice*, *volleyball*) and plurals (*snakes*) in general.
explanation in Latvian: Bez artikula: nosaukumi (*Rome*), neskaitāmi lietvārdi (*orange juice, volleyball*) un daudzskaitlis (*snakes*) vispārīgā nozīmē.

task: My daughter is afraid of ___, even small ones. (spider)
explanation shown to learner: No article with a plural noun when we mean all of them in general: *Spiders scare me.* With *the* it would mean some particular ones.
explanation in Latvian: Ar daudzskaitļa lietvārdu vispārīgā nozīmē (visi kopumā) artikulu nelieto: *Spiders scare me.* *the* norādītu uz kādiem noteiktiem.

task: In big cities, ___ are often faster than cars. (bike)
explanation shown to learner: No article with a plural noun when we mean all of them in general: *Spiders scare me.* With *the* it would mean some particular ones.
explanation in Latvian: Ar daudzskaitļa lietvārdu vispārīgā nozīmē (visi kopumā) artikulu nelieto: *Spiders scare me.* *the* norādītu uz kādiem noteiktiem.

task: ___ are cheaper than laptops. (tablet)
explanation shown to learner: No article with a plural noun when we mean all of them in general: *Spiders scare me.* With *the* it would mean some particular ones.
explanation in Latvian: Ar daudzskaitļa lietvārdu vispārīgā nozīmē (visi kopumā) artikulu nelieto: *Spiders scare me.* *the* norādītu uz kādiem noteiktiem.

task: ___ are my favourite flowers. (rose)
explanation shown to learner: No article with a plural noun when we mean all of them in general: *Spiders scare me.* With *the* it would mean some particular ones.
explanation in Latvian: Ar daudzskaitļa lietvārdu vispārīgā nozīmē (visi kopumā) artikulu nelieto: *Spiders scare me.* *the* norādītu uz kādiem noteiktiem.

task: My son collects ___. He has hundreds. (stamp)
explanation shown to learner: A hobby is about the things in general: *He collects stamps.* Plural, no article.
explanation in Latvian: Hobijs ir par lietām vispārīgi: *He collects stamps.* Daudzskaitlis, bez artikula.

task: Correct the mistake: My uncle works in the London.
explanation shown to learner: No article with names of people, cities and most countries: *Anna, Riga, Latvia*.
explanation in Latvian: Ar cilvēku, pilsētu un lielākās daļas valstu nosaukumiem artikulu nelieto: *Anna, Riga, Latvia.*

task: Correct the mistake: We play the basketball on Fridays.
correct answer: We play basketball on Fridays. | On Fridays we play basketball. | On fridays we play basketball.
explanation shown to learner: Sports and school subjects are uncountable nouns: no article (*play golf, teach maths*). But instruments take *the*: *play the piano*.
explanation in Latvian: Sporta veidi un skolas mācības (matemātika, vēsture) ir neskaitāmi lietvārdi: bez artikula (*play golf, teach maths*). Bet mūzikas instrumentiem vajag *the*: *play the piano*.

task: Correct the mistake: I eat the bread with every meal.
correct answer: I eat bread with every meal.
explanation shown to learner: *with every meal* = a habit, bread in general: no article.
explanation in Latvian: *with every meal* = ieradums, *bread* vispārīgā nozīmē: bez artikula.

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Choose the correct option: I ___ eat meat.
wrong options / checks: no more | any more | don't any more
explanation shown to learner: *no longer* goes before the verb: *I no longer eat meat.* *any more* goes at the end, after *don't*: *I don't eat meat any more.*
explanation in Latvian: *no longer* liek pirms darbības vārda: *I no longer eat meat.* *any more* liek beigās, aiz *don't*: *I don't eat meat any more.*

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Choose the correct option: She doesn't work here ___.
wrong options / checks: no more | no longer | more
explanation shown to learner: After a negative verb, use *any more* at the end: *She doesn't work here any more.* *no more* and *no longer* would add a second negative.
explanation in Latvian: Tulkojot burtiski vairs kā *more* vai *no more*, sanāk kļūda. Ja darbības vārds ir noliegumā, teikuma beigās liek *any more*: *She doesn't work here any more.*

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Which sentence is correct?
wrong options / checks: We are no more friends. | We aren't no longer friends. | We aren't friends no more.
explanation shown to learner: *no longer* goes after *be*, and *be* stays positive: *We are no longer friends.* Not *no more*, and not two negatives.
explanation in Latvian: Tulkojot burtiski, sanāk *no more* vai divkāršs noliegums. Angliski: *We are no longer friends*: aiz *are* liek *no longer*, un *are* nav noliegumā.

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Which sentence is correct?
correct answer: He no longer plays the guitar.
wrong options / checks: He plays no longer the guitar. | He no longer doesn't play the guitar. | He doesn't no longer play the guitar.
explanation shown to learner: *no longer* goes before the main verb, and the verb stays positive: *He no longer plays the guitar.*
explanation in Latvian: *no longer* liek pirms darbības vārda, un darbības vārds nav noliegumā: *He no longer plays the guitar.*

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: I don't live there no more.
wrong options / checks: My phone no longer works. | She isn't my boss any more. | We don't go to that gym any longer.
explanation shown to learner: Only one negative: *no longer* + a positive verb, or *don't* ... *any more* at the end. Not *don't ... no more*.
explanation in Latvian: Tulkojot burtiski vairs ne..., sanāk divkāršs noliegums (*I don't live there no more*). Angliski lieto vienu noliegumu: *I no longer live there* vai *I don't live there any more.*

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Choose the correct option: The bank ___ open on Saturdays.
wrong options / checks: is no more | no longer | is any more
explanation shown to learner: Keep *is* and put *no longer* after it: *The bank is no longer open.* Not *no more*; *any more* goes at the end, after *isn't*.
explanation in Latvian: Teikumā vajag *is*, un *no longer* liek aiz tā: *The bank is no longer open.* Nevis *no more; any more* liek beigās, aiz *isn't*.

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Choose the correct option: Tom moved to Oslo. He ___ lives in Riga.
wrong options / checks: still | any more | no more
explanation shown to learner: *still* = it continues; *no longer* = it has ended. Tom moved, so he *no longer* lives in Riga.
explanation in Latvian: *still* = joprojām turpinās; *no longer* = ir beidzies. Viņš pārcēlās, tāpēc: *He no longer lives in Riga.*

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Complete with one word: My sister doesn't live with us any ___.
explanation shown to learner: *any more* or *any longer*: both go at the end, after a negative verb.
explanation in Latvian: *any more* vai *any longer*: abi liek teikuma beigās, ja darbības vārds ir noliegumā.

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Complete with one word: I no ___ use this app.
explanation shown to learner: *no longer* goes before the verb: *I no longer use this app.* We don't say *no more* here.
explanation in Latvian: *no longer* liek pirms darbības vārda: *I no longer use this app.* Šeit nelieto *no more*.

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Write *no longer* or *any more*: The airline ___ flies to Riga.
explanation shown to learner: *flies* is positive, so *no longer* goes before it. *any more* needs a negative verb and goes at the end.
explanation in Latvian: *flies* nav noliegumā, tāpēc pirms tā liek *no longer*. *any more* vajag noliegumu, un to liek beigās.

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Write *no longer* or *any more*: We don't go camping ___.
explanation shown to learner: *don't* is already negative, so *any more* goes at the end: *We don't go camping any more.*
explanation in Latvian: *don't* jau ir noliegums, tāpēc beigās liek *any more*: *We don't go camping any more.*

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Complete with one word: They're ___ longer married.
explanation shown to learner: *no longer*, not *not longer*: *They're no longer married.* (= *They aren't married any more.*)
explanation in Latvian: *no longer*, nevis *not longer*: *They're no longer married.* (= *They aren't married any more*.)

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Say it another way with *no longer*: I don't work there any more.
correct answer: I no longer work there. | I am no longer working there. | I'm no longer working there.
explanation shown to learner: *don't ... any more* = *no longer* before a positive verb: *I no longer work there.*
explanation in Latvian: *don't* ... *any more = no longer* + darbības vārds, kas nav noliegumā: *I no longer work there.*

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Say it another way with *no longer*: The museum isn't free any more.
correct answer: The museum is no longer free. | The museum's no longer free.
explanation shown to learner: *isn't ... any more* = *is no longer*: *no longer* goes after *is*, and *is* stays positive.
explanation in Latvian: *isn't* ... *any more = is no longer*: *no longer* liek aiz *is*, un *is* nav noliegumā.

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Say it another way with *any more*: Ben no longer studies Spanish.
correct answer: Ben doesn't study Spanish any more. | Ben doesn't study Spanish anymore. | Ben isn't studying Spanish any more. | Ben isn't studying Spanish anymore. | Ben's not studying Spanish any more. | Ben's not studying Spanish anymore.
explanation shown to learner: *no longer studies* = *doesn't study* ... *any more*: the verb becomes negative and *any more* goes at the end.
explanation in Latvian: *no longer studies = doesn't study* ... *any more*: darbības vārds ir noliegumā, un *any more* liek beigās.

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Put the words in order.
explanation shown to learner: *no longer* goes before the main verb, and the verb stays positive: *He no longer plays the guitar.*
explanation in Latvian: *no longer* liek pirms darbības vārda, un darbības vārds nav noliegumā: *He no longer plays the guitar.*

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: we're no longer in the same team
explanation shown to learner: With *be*, *no longer* goes after it: *We're no longer in the same team.*
explanation in Latvian: Ja teikumā ir *be, no longer* liek aiz tā: *We're no longer in the same team.*

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: my old printer no longer works
explanation shown to learner: *no longer* goes before the main verb, and the verb stays positive: *He no longer plays the guitar.*
explanation in Latvian: *no longer* liek pirms darbības vārda, un darbības vārds nav noliegumā: *He no longer plays the guitar.*

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: i don't drive to work any more
explanation shown to learner: *any more* (or *any longer*) goes at the end, after a negative verb: *I don't drive to work any more.*
explanation in Latvian: *any more* (vai *any longer*) liek teikuma beigās, ja darbības vārds ir noliegumā: *I don't drive to work any more.*

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: he's not my neighbour any longer
explanation shown to learner: *any more* (or *any longer*) goes at the end, after a negative verb: *I don't drive to work any more.*
explanation in Latvian: *any more* (vai *any longer*) liek teikuma beigās, ja darbības vārds ir noliegumā: *I don't drive to work any more.*

topic: Used to and be used to
task: She is ___ my teacher.
wrong options / checks: bank: no longer | no more | any more
explanation shown to learner: After *is*, use *no longer*: *She is no longer my teacher.* *any more* goes at the end after *isn't*; *no more* is not used here.
explanation in Latvian: Tulkojot burtiski vairs kā *no more*, sanāk kļūda. Aiz *is* liek *no longer*: *She is no longer my teacher.* *any more* liek beigās aiz *isn't*.

topic: Used to and be used to
task: We don't use cash ___ ___.
wrong options / checks: bank: any | no | more
explanation shown to learner: *don't* is already negative, so the end is *any more*, not *no more*.
explanation in Latvian: *don't* jau ir noliegums, tāpēc beigās ir *any more*, nevis *no more*.

topic: Used to and be used to
task: This bus ___ goes to the airport.
wrong options / checks: bank: no longer | any more | no more
explanation shown to learner: Before a positive verb, use *no longer*: *This bus no longer goes to the airport.* *any more* goes at the end, after *doesn't*.
explanation in Latvian: Ja darbības vārds nav noliegumā, pirms tā liek *no longer*: *This bus no longer goes to the airport.* *any more* liek beigās, aiz *doesn't*.

topic: Used to and be used to
task: These shoes ___ comfortable ___.
wrong options / checks: bank: aren't | are | any more
explanation shown to learner: *any more* needs a negative verb: *These shoes aren't comfortable any more.*
explanation in Latvian: *any more* lieto ar noliegumu: *These shoes aren't comfortable any more.*

topic: Used to and be used to
task: Match each beginning with its ending.
correct answer: He no longer = plays football. ; She is no longer = our manager. ; They don't live here = any more. ; We aren't = neighbours any longer.
explanation shown to learner: *no longer* before the verb (*He no longer plays*) or after *be* (*She is no longer*); *any more / any longer* at the end, after a negative verb.
explanation in Latvian: *no longer* pirms darbības vārda (*He no longer plays*) vai aiz *be* (*She is no longer*); *any more / any longer* beigās, ja darbības vārds ir noliegumā.

task: Choose the correct option: Could you ___ the window, please?
wrong options / checks: to open | opening | opens
explanation shown to learner: After *can / could / would / may* comes the base verb, without *to* or *-ing*: *Could you open the window?* (not *Could you to open*).
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *can / could / would / may* ir darbības vārda pamatforma bez to un bez *-ing*: *Could you open the window?* (nevis *Could you to open*).

task: Which sentence is correct?
correct answer: Would you check my email, please?
wrong options / checks: Would you to check my email, please? | Would you checking my email, please? | Would you checked my email, please?
explanation shown to learner: After *can / could / would / may* comes the base verb, without *to* or *-ing*: *Would you check my email?* (not *Would you to check*).
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *can / could / would / may* ir darbības vārda pamatforma bez to un bez *-ing*: *Would you check my email?* (nevis *Would you to check*).

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: May you help me with this form?
wrong options / checks: May I use your charger? | Could you call me back later? | Can I try this jacket on?
explanation shown to learner: *May* asks for permission with *I*: *May I use your charger?* To ask somebody to do something, say *Can / Could / Would you…?*: *Could you help me with this form?* The other sentences are correct.
explanation in Latvian: *May* lieto atļaujas lūgšanai ar *I*: *May I use your charger?* Lūdzot, lai cits cilvēks kaut ko izdarītu, saka *Can / Could / Would you*…?: *Could you help me with this form?* Pārējie teikumi ir bez kļūdām.

task: Choose the correct option: Can I ___ a coffee and a croissant, please?
wrong options / checks: to have | having
explanation shown to learner: To ask for something: *Can I have…?* (or *Could I have…?*), with the base verb: *Can I have a coffee, please?*
explanation in Latvian: Lūdzot kaut ko saņemt: *Can I have*…? (vai *Could I have*…?) ar pamatformu: *Can I have a coffee, please?*

task: Which sentence is correct?
correct answer: Can I borrow your pen for a moment?
wrong options / checks: Can you borrow me your pen for a moment? | Can I to borrow your pen for a moment? | Can I lend your pen for a moment?
explanation shown to learner: *Can I borrow your pen?* = I take it and give it back later. *Can you lend me your pen?* = you give it to me for a short time. Not *borrow me*, not *Can I lend…?*
explanation in Latvian: *Can I borrow your pen?* = es aizņemos (paņemu uz laiku). *Can you lend me your pen?* = jūs man aizdodat. Nevis *borrow me*, nevis *Can I lend*…?

task: Which sentence is correct?
correct answer: May I see your passport, please?
wrong options / checks: May I to see your passport, please? | May I seeing your passport, please? | May you show me your passport, please?
explanation shown to learner: *May I* + base verb asks for permission politely: *May I see your passport?* There is no *May you…?* request: *Could you show me your passport?*
explanation in Latvian: *May I* + pamatforma pieklājīgi lūdz atļauju: *May I see your passport?* Lūgums *May you*…? nepastāv: *Could you show me your passport?*

task: Which sentence is correct?
correct answer: Can you give me a lift to work?
wrong options / checks: Do you can give me a lift to work? | Can you to give me a lift to work? | Can you giving me a lift to work?
explanation shown to learner: A question with *can* needs no *do*: *Can you* + base verb: *Can you give me a lift?* (not *Do you can…?*).
explanation in Latvian: Jautājumā ar *can* nelieto *do*: *Can you* + pamatforma: *Can you give me a lift?* (nevis *Do you can*…?).

task: Could you ___ this word to me? (explain)
explanation shown to learner: After *can / could / would / may* comes the base verb, without *to* or *-ing*: *Could you explain this word?* (not *Could you to explain*).
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *can / could / would / may* ir darbības vārda pamatforma bez to un bez *-ing*: *Could you explain this word?* (nevis *Could you to explain*).

task: Write the missing word: Can ___ borrow your charger? Mine is at home.
explanation shown to learner: *Can I…?* asks if I may do something: *Can I borrow your charger?* (I take it for a short time). *Mine is at home* shows who needs it.
explanation in Latvian: *Can I*…? jautā, vai es drīkstu kaut ko darīt: *Can I borrow your charger?* (es aizņemos uz laiku). *Mine is at home* parāda, ka lādētājs vajadzīgs man.

task: Would you ___ quiet, please? I'm on the phone. (be)
explanation shown to learner: After *can / could / would / may* comes the base verb, without *to* or *-ing*: *Would you be quiet, please?* (not *Would you are quiet*).
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *can / could / would / may* ir darbības vārda pamatforma bez to un bez *-ing*: *Would you be quiet, please?* (nevis *Would you are quiet*).

task: Write the missing word: 'Can I take a photo of your garden?' 'Yes, go ___.'
explanation shown to learner: To say yes to *Can I…?*: *Yes, go ahead.* (also *Sure.* or *Yes, of course.*).
explanation in Latvian: Lai atļautu (atbilde uz *Can I*…?): *Yes, go ahead.* (arī *Sure*. vai *Yes, of course*.).

task: Could your sister ___ me to the airport tomorrow? (take)
explanation shown to learner: After *could* the verb has no *-s*, also with *he / she*: *Could your sister take me?* (not *takes*).

task: Last summer we went ___ in the forest.
wrong options / checks: bank: camping | to camping | for camping
explanation shown to learner: *go* + *-ing* for activities, with nothing in between: *go fishing, go skiing, go camping*. Not *go to fishing* or *go for fishing*.
explanation in Latvian: *go + -ing* nodarbēm, bez nekā starp tiem: *go fishing, go skiing, go camping*. Nevis *go to fishing* vai *go for fishing*.

task: It's late, so I'm going ___.
wrong options / checks: bank: home | to home | at home
explanation shown to learner: *go home*, not *go to home* or *go at home*: *I'm going home.*
explanation in Latvian: Saka *go home*, nevis *go to home* vai *go at home*: *I'm going home.*

task: Let's go ___ a ___ before dinner.
wrong options / checks: bank: for | run | to | running
explanation shown to learner: *go running* (*-ing*, no *for*) = *go for a run* (*a* + noun). Not *go for running*.
explanation in Latvian: *go running* (*-ing*, bez *for*) = *go for a run* (*a* + lietvārds). Nevis *go for running*.

task: Match each beginning with its ending.
correct answer: Let's go for = a coffee after work. ; She goes to = the gym every morning. ; We're going on = holiday in July. ; They often go = fishing at the weekend.
explanation shown to learner: *go* + *-ing* (*go fishing*), *go for a* + noun (*go for a coffee*), *go to* + place (*go to the gym*), *go on holiday*, *go home*.
explanation in Latvian: *go + -ing* (*go fishing*), *go for a* + lietvārds (*go for a coffee*), *go to* + vieta (*go to the gym*), *go on holiday, go home*.
